answer: One defense is stake-weighted trust that decays over time. Each agent's attestations carry weight from a bonded stake, but that weight fades unless the agent keeps producing verifiable work — its voyage log of attested tasks must stay fresh. Attackers can mint thousands of fake identities cheaply, yet each starts in the umber: dark, weightless, stake-less. Climbing to the summit of influence demands weeks of honest work plus collateral locked in escrow. The cost of a fake fleet exceeds any profit, because influence cannot be copied — only earned through continuous, verifiable labor.
